approach: Same placement as round 1, with a trigger and a Timeline test rebuilt from the class and each finding answered. Add one refusal check, `check_timing_claim(reading, request)`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs, wired as one `step!` line in `refusing_check` (reading/checks.rs:520-551) right after `check_records_measure` (checks.rs:541). It uses the shared gate `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion` (surveys.rs:237). Per segment (`sentences`, checks.rs:332) of the request without Athena-generated lines, the summary and the criteria, it fires on a speed, delay or cut phrase with a duration figure, or a strong speed phrase with a stage noun, or a cut verb with a time word and a stage noun. Inflected forms are listed explicitly, as `requires_existing_code_section` lists REUSE (surveys.rs:1360-1369). A refusal-rule reading (a criterion declares `newly refused` and a deliverable is a reading-check file) is exempt. The reading must then carry a `Timeline:` assumption with a real crates/ path, at least two duration figures, a stage-order marker, a source label and a claimed-figure word. The error text is the information the reader lacks. It lists the pipeline stage order from `StageMinutes::named` (status/throughput.rs:113), says where measured durations live, asks whether the request's own figure matches, and gives an example whose path exists. Nothing is added to the reader prompt: its set is 1998 of 2000 tokens (docs/system-facts.md). CHANGELOG.md and a new D190 name the root cause. Findings: (1) the vocabulary is built from the class (decision 3), and each existing Accept case is decided on purpose (decision 4). (2) `shorten` needs a time word (decision 3). (3) The exemption is narrowed (decision 2). (4) The example path is `crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs`, and a test checks it on disk (decision 5). (5) The error names the status medians and asks for a match statement or an `unchecked estimate` label (decision 5). (6) The INPUT_FORMS length is 63 + 14 = 77 (decision 7). (7) The declaration test wraps the sentence in a Criterion (decision 9).

decisions.choice: Fix it at the reading gate, as a refusal whose error text carries the missing information, and add no prompt or reader-rule line.
decisions.reason: The failing stage lacked the real stage order and measured durations when it accepted a speed or delay figure from the request. The reader prompt cannot take a rule line: its always-loaded set is 1998 of 2000 tokens (docs/system-facts.md budget reader), and `READING_RULES.len() == 14` is pinned in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs (read in round 1, test `the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line`). So the information goes to the reader as the correction text of the second read (`read_once`, reading.rs:732-741 and 750-771). That text lists the six stages in pipeline order from `StageMinutes::named` (status/throughput.rs:113: reading, planning, producer, checks, verifier, landing and rebuild). It says `athena status` prints their medians per landed job (the steward's slowdown request already quotes them, hestia.rs:2398-2407). It says what to write, and gives an example. The check proves the Timeline is present, not that its figures are true.

rejected.option: A rule line in READING_RULES or an edit to crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md
rejected.why: The reader set has 2 tokens left, and the rule-line count test pins 14 lines. `check_history_fixture` has no rule line either.

rejected.option: Run the code or read records inside the check to measure the stages
rejected.why: The check sees the reading and request only, as its siblings do (surveys.rs:199, 538). The reader has no records (docs/system-facts.md, plain copy).

decisions.choice: Gate with `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`. Scan the request without generated lines, the summary and every criterion. Exempt only a refusal-rule reading: a criterion contains `newly refused` and a non-deleted deliverable path starts with `crates/athena-core/src/reading` or is `crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs`.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. The sibling `records_measure_trigger` skips only the declaring criterion (surveys.rs:452-460). That fits a records-measure rule, whose own criteria rarely need measure words. A speed-claim rule must describe test requests such as `move a call earlier to save about 12 minutes` in its criteria, so a refusal-rule reading (this job's own included) would be asked for a timeline of a pipeline it does not change. A declaration alone is not enough, though: a reading that changes `gh.rs` and adds `expected 4% of newly refused readings` would otherwise skip the check. The path bound closes that, and a corpus case pairs the exempt reading with the same declaration on a pipeline file, which is refused. The request is scanned because the figure enters there, but lines Athena generated are dropped with `is_generated_line(line, request.contains(ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR), false)` (terms.rs:50-80, reachable through `pub use terms::*`, reading.rs:72). The `Failure class:`, `Cause:` and `Introspection … prevention it proposed:` lines of a root-cause request quote old records. A root-cause job on an unrelated class is therefore not asked for a timeline because a quoted prevention says `speed-up` beside `tests`. The same helper is used by `plain_request_prose` (terms.rs:189-204).

rejected.option: Exempt any reading that declares `newly refused`
rejected.why: It is a bypass: add the declaration to a speed-up reading and the check is skipped.

rejected.option: Skip only the declaring criterion, as the sibling does
rejected.why: A refusal-rule reading for this check has criteria such as the 8hzb-style request, so it would need a fake Timeline.

rejected.option: Scan the reading only, not the request
rejected.why: A reader that drops the figure from the summary would hide the claim. The figure enters in the request.

decisions.choice: Build the trigger from the class in three rules on one segment (lowercase, hyphen and underscore read as a space, whole-word `has_phrase`, surveys.rs:39). T1: any SPEED, DELAY or CUT phrase and a duration figure. T2: a SPEED phrase and a STAGE noun. T3: a CUT verb, a TIME word and a STAGE noun. Lists: SPEED = speed up, speeds up, sped up, speeding up, speedup, faster, quicker, slower, too slow, slow down, slows, slowed, slowing, slowdown, takes longer, take longer, taking longer, took longer. DELAY (figure only) = slow, delay, delays, delayed, delaying, sooner, and `earlier` unless the next word is job, jobs, attempt, attempts, round, rounds, version, commit, commits, record, records, review, plan, reading, result, results, run, runs, failure, request or retry. CUT = reduce, reduces, reduced, reducing, cut, cuts, cutting, save, saves, saved, saving, shave, shaves, shaved, shaving, shorten, shortens, shortened, shortening. TIME = time, times, wait, waits, waiting, duration, durations, latency, runtime. STAGE = pipeline, pipelines, test suite, test, tests, ci, check, checks, compile, compilation, build, builds, stage, stages, planning, reading, producer, verifier, landing. A duration figure is a number with a unit (s, sec, secs, second, seconds, ms, millisecond, milliseconds, min, mins, minute, minutes, h, hr, hrs, hour, hours), spaced or glued (`90s`, `500ms`).
decisions.reason: Answers findings 1 and 2. `has_phrase` matches whole words only, so the inflections must be listed. `delayed` plus `12 minutes` and `Reduce the CI wait from 10 minutes` fire T1. `speeds up the tests` fires T2. The steward's own slowdown request (`now takes longer`, `stage`, `45.0 min`, hestia.rs:2398-2413) fires T2 and T1. `Reduce time spent waiting for CI` fires T3. `shorten` is only a CUT verb, so it never fires with a stage noun alone: `Shorten the reader prompt so the budget tests pass` has no TIME word and no figure and is accepted (HISTORY.txt:737 shows `shorten` is mostly about text). `delay`, `sooner` and `earlier` need a figure, since `delay` also names code behavior and `earlier job` and `earlier attempt` are ordinary prose (refusal_corpus.rs:267-274). The words `run` and `throughput` are not triggers: every behavior criterion says `Run `cargo test``. A grep of crates/**/tests, reading.rs and src/**/*.rs found no fixture that reaches the gate with these phrases, apart from the steward text, `fake::SPEED_WORDS` and the `ci-wait` case below.

rejected.option: Only the words of the three cited jobs (speed up, faster, delay, earlier, shorten)
rejected.why: It misses `delayed`, `speeds up`, `slows`, `takes longer` and `Reduce the CI wait`, so the class is only partly prevented.
It is the fake reader's urgency list for a different purpose (it holds `timeouts`, `thrash` and `wasted time`), and it lives in a test double.

rejected.option: Count `shorten` or `reduce` with a stage noun alone
rejected.why: It would refuse prompt-length and token-budget work that mentions tests.

decisions.choice: Decide each existing records-measure Accept case on purpose. `ci-wait-time-spent-reading` (refusal_corpus.rs:482-490) becomes `Expected::Refuse("check_timing_claim")`. `ci-drain-throughput-reading` (473-481) stays Accept.
decisions.reason: `Reduce time spent waiting for CI` is the class itself: it is a CUT verb with a TIME word and the stage noun `ci`, and the 8hzb job was a CI-wait speed-up. The case stays valid for its old purpose, because the corpus asserts the first refusing check and `check_records_measure` still does not refuse it. A new case `ci-wait-time-spent-with-timeline` accepts the same reading once it carries a Timeline. The unit test `records_measure_leaves_unrelated_readings_alone` (reading.rs:8642-8649) uses `assert_ne!(gate_refuser(..), Some("check_records_measure"))`, so it needs no edit. `Raise the throughput of the drain queue` names no stage duration, time word or claimed delay, so there is nothing for a timeline to check. `throughput` stays out of the trigger on purpose, and the doc comment's Limits say so. This changes the expectation of one existing corpus case, which criterion 4 allows because the corpus test passes with its new expectation.

rejected.option: Keep `ci-wait-time-spent-reading` as Accept by exempting speed requests that carry no figure
rejected.why: It is a speed request about a pipeline stage, so exempting it leaves the class half-open.
It matches every queue or capacity change and overlaps `check_records_measure`'s throughput phrases.

decisions.choice: Judge the best `Timeline:` assumption (label matched after trim, any case, as `code_surveys`, surveys.rs:117-124) by five lexical parts: (a) a `crates/` path (`names_crates_path`, surveys.rs:127); (b) at least two duration figures; (c) a stage-order marker (`then`, `->`, `→`, `=>`, `before`, `after`, `followed by`; the arrows are matched before hyphens become spaces); (d) a source label (`measured`, `recorded`, `estimate`, `estimated`); (e) a claim word (`claimed` or `claim`). The error names the trigger and where it was found, the missing parts of the nearest Timeline, and one example.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 4 and 5. The example ends `for example: "Timeline: crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs runs reading 3 min (recorded), then planning 9 min (recorded), then producer 14 min (recorded), then checks 6 min (recorded), then verifier 8 min (estimate); the claimed 12 minute delay sits in checks". ` followed by one more sentence. It has no double quote and avoids words other checks scan for, such as pull request, cache and push. `crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs` exists (Glob of crates/athena-core/src/run/). There is no `run.rs`, so the round-1 path would have been refused by `check_reading_references` (checks.rs:408-473), which `read_once` runs with the real file set (reading.rs:732-738). The example test checks that every path token of the example exists on disk under CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../.. (precedent: admission.rs:1622) and then runs `check_reading_references` with a set built from those paths. The error text also says: the stages in pipeline order are those of `StageMinutes::named`; the measured medians are printed by `athena status` (a reader with no records takes them from the request, or from timeouts and poll intervals in the code); say in the Timeline whether the request's own figure matches the stage durations, or label it an `unchecked estimate` (the word `estimate` satisfies (d)). It also says that a stage the request named but the code does not run in that order is the usual error.

rejected.option: Accept any `Timeline:` assumption that names a crates/ path
rejected.why: It is `check_code_survey`'s weakness (surveys.rs:203-206): an empty timeline with a path would pass.

rejected.option: A model call to judge the timeline
rejected.why: The mechanism default asks for code, and a model call would not be deterministic in the replay.

The order doc of `check_reading_acceptance` (checks.rs:475-491) gains [`check_timing_claim`].

No test pins the successor of `check_records_measure`: the order tests pin only the predecessor of `check_history_fixture` and `check_records_measure` (reading.rs:8698-8722 and the history one).

Add 14 tags to INPUT_FORMS, so the array length goes from 63 (line 90) to 77. Changing the list means recounting.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 6: 14 new tags are timing-claim-with-figure, timing-claim-stage-noun, timing-claim-inflected-form, timing-claim-reduce-verb, timing-claim-hyphen-spelling, timeline-assumption-satisfied, timeline-missing-parts, timing-claim-generated-root-cause-lines, refusal-rule-declaration-exempt, refusal-declaration-on-pipeline-change, docs-class-speed-claim, shorten-text-not-time, steward-slowdown-request and earlier-as-adjective. Input forms and cases (all new unless an id is quoted): (1) dash bullet with figure and no Timeline, `timing-claim-call-earlier-12-minutes-no-timeline`, Refuse(check_timing_claim). (2) The same with a satisfying Timeline, `timing-claim-call-earlier-12-minutes-with-timeline`, Accept. (3) Star bullet with a stage noun and no figure, `timing-claim-speed-up-the-tests-star-bullet`, Refuse. (4) Numbered `1.` part, `timing-claim-reduce-ci-wait-numbered-part`, Refuse. `1)` and `(a)` parts are read as the `1.` part is, because the rule splits on newlines and does not parse markers. `1)` and `(a)` get no case of their own, and the existing `delivery-verb-in-a-numbered-paren-part` pattern (refusal_corpus.rs:936) covers the parser. (5) Inflections `delayed by 12 minutes` and `speeds up the test suite`, `timing-claim-delayed-and-speeds-up`, Refuse. (6) Hyphen spelling `speed-up` with `90s`, `timing-claim-hyphen-spelling-90s`, Refuse. (7) Existing `ci-wait-time-spent-reading`, changed to Refuse. (8) New `ci-wait-time-spent-with-timeline`, Accept. (9) Existing `ci-drain-throughput-reading`, unchanged Accept. (10) Timeline with a path and no durations or order, `timing-claim-timeline-without-durations`, Refuse. (11) Word inside another word, `timing-claim-word-inside-delayer` (`delayer` with a figure), Accept; tag trigger-word-inside-other-word. (12) Docs-class reading with a speed claim, `timing-claim-docs-reading`, Accept. (13) Refusal-rule reading with the declaration and a reading-check deliverable, `timing-claim-refusal-rule-declaration-exempt`, Accept. (14) The same declaration with `crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs`, `timing-claim-declaration-on-pipeline-change`, Refuse. (15) A root-cause request built by the real `athena_core::hestia::root_cause_request` (as `generated_root_cause_request`, refusal_corpus.rs:1327) whose cause and prevention quote `speed-up`, `faster` and `12 minutes`, with a neutral code reading, `timing-claim-generated-root-cause-quotes-only`, Accept; tags cites-job-without-relying and timing-claim-generated-root-cause-lines. (16) `Shorten the reader prompt so the budget tests pass`, `timing-claim-shorten-prompt-with-tests`, Accept. (17) A steward request built by the real `athena_core::hestia::slowdown_request`, `timing-claim-steward-slowdown-request`, Refuse, and the same with a Timeline, `timing-claim-steward-slowdown-with-timeline`, Accept. (18) A retry complaint (existing pattern, refusal_corpus.rs:1953-1972) whose text says `the earlier attempt ran 40 minutes` with a code reading, `timing-claim-retry-earlier-attempt-figure`, Accept; tags retry-complaint and earlier-as-adjective. Not applicable: a crate-relative bare path, a governance path and a brand word. The rule reads phrases, not paths or symbols, and the Timeline's path test reuses `names_crates_path`, covered by the code-survey cases. Run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` as a demonstration; no result is claimed here.

decisions.choice: Exits of the new stage `check_timing_claim` (a pure function of `reading` and `request`). Exit success, no claim, gate closed or exempt: returns Ok; `step!` falls through (checks.rs:528-533) to `check_design_existing_code` (checks.rs:542); no state is left. Exit success, claim with a satisfying Timeline: same. Exit fail, claim with no satisfying Timeline: returns Err; `step!` returns `Some(("check_timing_claim", error))` (checks.rs:530). `read_once` turns it into `Err((rule, text))` (reading.rs:740), stores a `ReadingAttempt` with the redacted refusal (reading.rs:760-770), and the reader reads once more with the text as its correction. `check_reading_acceptance` returns the error to the other callers (checks.rs:499-502): plan, drain, the steward's `queued_work` and `check_reading_text` (replay.rs:54-65). Status counts the refusal under the rule name. Exit error (I/O): cannot happen; no file, git, network or record is read. Exit hold: cannot happen in this stage. The replay hold (a newly refused share above the declared share plus 5 points) acts later, in verification (replay.rs:159-165 and 293-295). Exit interrupt: cannot happen; the function is synchronous and reads no kill switch.
decisions.reason: The required exit table for a changed core flow, with the handling code of each exit.

decisions.choice: Declare the share in criterion text and the doc comment, and test the doc and the parse separately. The doc comment above `pub fn check_timing_claim(` (a block of `///` lines with no attribute) holds `This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.` and `expected 4% of newly refused readings` marked as an estimate: 3 of about 1000 scored jobs recorded the class, about 2 of the last 200 commit subjects name a speed topic (HISTORY.txt:737 and :1137) and neither is a timing claim, and the replay at verification measures the real share. It adds `Limits:` naming: lexical, no reading of negation; figures written as words (`a minute`) are not read, so a request with no figure and no stage noun is missed; `earlier`, `delay` and `slow` need a figure; `earlier` before a noun such as attempt or job is not a trigger; `throughput` and capacity requests are not read; a Timeline proves presence, not that its figures are true, and an `estimate` label passes; the exemption is bounded to reading-check deliverables.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 7. `replay_declaration(criteria: &[Criterion], out_of_scope)` (replay.rs:263) parses criterion text through `declared_percent` (replay.rs:227-252: a whole percent tied to `newly refused`), not doc comments. The test `timing_claim_refusal_is_declared_intended` therefore (a) wraps the sentence `The change refuses more readings: expected 4% of newly refused readings` in a `Criterion` and asserts `share == Some(4)`, as refusal_corpus.rs:3140-3147 does; (b) asserts the doc-comment needles as text; (c) wraps the whole doc in a Criterion and asserts 4, as lines 3179-3186 do; (d) asserts the CHANGELOG and D190 needles. The reader brief asks for the same sentence (crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs:371). The 4% figure is the user-accepted estimate; the broader trigger could raise the real share, which the replay measures against the declared share plus 5 points.

risks.risk: The lexical trigger refuses a reading it should not (a stage noun beside `faster` in an unrelated sentence, `reduce the timeout to 30 seconds` as a config change), or misses a claim stated in words (`a minute`) with no stage noun.
risks.mitigation: Every rule needs a speed, delay or cut phrase plus a figure or a stage noun in one segment, and only code or tests readings with a behavior criterion are gated. `shorten` and `reduce` need a time word, and `earlier`, `delay` and `slow` need a figure. `earlier` before a noun, generated request lines and refusal-rule readings are excluded. The doc `Limits:` names the rest. The replay at verification measures the share against the declared 4% plus 5 points and sends the list of newly refused jobs back to the producer, who narrows the tables.

risks.risk: The declared 4% is an estimate. The broader class vocabulary (inflections, reduce verbs, stage nouns) could refuse more than the three jobs suggest.
risks.mitigation: The estimate is labeled as such in the doc comment, D190 and the CHANGELOG, with its basis (3 of about 1000 scored jobs; about 2 of the last 200 commit subjects name a speed topic and neither is a timing claim). The replay measures the real share and holds the job above 9% with the offending job ids; the number is not claimed as measured.

risks.risk: A Timeline can pass the lexical parts with invented figures or an `estimate` label, because the reader has no records.
risks.mitigation: This is stated in the doc comment's `Limits:` and in D190. The error text gives the real stage order and the place of the medians, asks whether the request's figure matches, and offers the `unchecked estimate` label. The planner's and critic's prose rules and the verifier running the criteria remain the guard on truth.

risks.risk: The gate short-circuits, so a gate-level test request may be refused first by another check (for example `check_outcome_state` for delivery words or `check_defined_terms` for ladder, rung, tier or layer), and the example text may trip an environment or boundary check.
risks.mitigation: The producer picks request and example wording those checks do not refuse and asserts the refusing check by name with `refuser_for`; the example test pushes the example through the whole gate (as reading.rs:8548-8550 does for the sibling) and through `check_reading_references` with the real paths.

risks.risk: Changing the expectation of the existing corpus case `ci-wait-time-spent-reading` from Accept to Refuse looks like a regression of an earlier decision.
risks.mitigation: It was an Accept case only because no check read speed claims; it is the class itself. The case keeps its id, source and tags, still proves `check_records_measure` does not refuse it, and the change is stated in decision 4, D190 and the CHANGELOG entry.

risks.risk: The generated-line skip relies on the generator's anchor sentence and line prefixes; if `root_cause_request_at` changes its text, quoted introspection lines would be scanned.
risks.mitigation: The corpus case `timing-claim-generated-root-cause-quotes-only` is built from the real `hestia::root_cause_request`, so a generator change fails it. `plain_request_prose` (terms.rs:189) already depends on the same anchor.

It reads the source through `reading_source()` and asserts: exactly one `step!(check_timing_claim(reading, request));` line sits in the body of `refusing_check`, immediately after the `step!(check_records_measure(reading));` line; the source holds `pub fn check_timing_claim(reading: &Reading, request: &str) -> Result<()>`; the text above `pub fn check_reading_acceptance(` names [`check_timing_claim`]; and the error of a refusing fixture (from `check_timing_claim(..).unwrap_err()`) contains `` `Timeline:` ``, `for example`, `athena status` and `landing and rebuild`.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in the reading.rs test module, next to the records-measure tests. (1) `timing_claim_without_timeline_is_refused_and_with_timeline_accepted`: build `code_reading(&[SURVEY], &[MODIFY_READING])` (reading.rs:7049-7081), set the summary to `Move the call earlier in the run to save about 12 minutes`, and use that sentence as the request. Assert `refuser_for(&reading, request) == Some("check_timing_claim")` (reading.rs:7300), that `check_timing_claim(&reading, request).unwrap_err()` equals the gate's error text, and that `check_reading_text(&reading, request)` is `Refuse` with the Timeline text. Then push a `Timeline:` assumption naming `crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs`, stages in order with durations and the claimed delay, and assert `refuser_for` is None, `accept` is Ok and `check_reading_text` is `Accept`. (2) `timing_claim_class_shapes_are_refused`: a table of request and summary pairs for the class, not the one job: the 8hzb shape, `Speed up the test suite` (c453 and eebk shape, no figure), `The checks are delayed by 12 minutes`, `This speeds up the tests`, `Reduce the CI wait from 10 minutes`, `Reduce time spent waiting for CI`, `speed-up`, `Speed Up`, `90s`, `500ms`, and the text of the real generator `crate::hestia::slowdown_request(25.0, 60.0, &[StageGrowth{stage:"producer", previous_minutes:25.0, minutes:45.0}])` (hestia.rs:2381, 2320). Each is refused by check_timing_claim. (3) `timing_claim_leaves_other_readings_alone`: no speed or delay claim (the default `code_reading`), `delayer` with a figure, `Shorten the reader prompt so the budget tests pass`, `Raise the throughput of the drain queue`, `the earlier attempt ran 40 minutes`, a docs class, a question, a decline, content-only criteria, a root-cause request from `crate::hestia::root_cause_request` whose quoted lines hold the words, and a reading with `expected 4% of newly refused readings` and a `crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs` deliverable. Each gives `refuser_for != Some("check_timing_claim")`; and the same declaration with `crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs` is refused. (4) `timing_claim_names_each_missing_timeline_part`: remove the path, the second figure, the order marker, the label and the claim word one at a time; each refuses and names the missing part. (5) `timing_claim_example_satisfies_the_check_and_names_real_files`: extract the example as at reading.rs:8543-8547, push it as an assumption and assert the gate gives None; split it with `sentences` and `path_tokens`, assert every `crates/` token exists under `Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../..")`, and assert `check_reading_references(&reading, Some(&files))` is Ok for a set made of those paths.
demonstrations.observes: The 8hzb-style reading with a claim and no Timeline is refused by `check_timing_claim` with an error naming `Timeline:`; it is accepted once a Timeline holds the path, order, durations, label and claim word.
